findings.what: nb_try SUCCESS TEST NEVER FIRES. kaggle 2.2.4 prints only 'N submissions remaining today.' after a successful kernel submit. The server message is empty, and cli.py does print(out, end=''). 'Successfully submitted' is absent from every real submit in the session transcripts (~40 submits, 6 Sep - 28 Sep 12:15Z). Errors come from kagglesdk as HTTPError(resp['message']): the server text, with no status code, goes to stderr with exit 1. Consequences: (a) R27N-4 nb_try treats every success as 'no match'. It self-heals on the next pass (sleep 30 s, list, ALREADY -> return 0), but the batch log reads like a failure. (b) R27N-3's 'Expect Successfully submitted. Any other output: do NOT resubmit blindly' makes the operator misread every success. (c) The HARD FAIL pattern '40[0134]' may never match a JSON-body error. nb_try v3 (in the checklist) fixes all three. Success = rc 0 AND '[0-9]+ submissions remaining today'. The checks then run network (incl. rc 124, 'Max retries', 429, 'rate limit') -> daily-limit (daily|allowance|submission limit|per day|tomorrow|exceeded; exit 3) -> hard fail (not found|could not find|forbidden|permission|unauthori|does not exist|40x) -> UNKNOWN = list first. Bonus: the remaining-today count is a free used_today check.
findings.evidence: site-packages kaggle/api/kaggle_api_extended.py competition_submit_cli (prints f'{limits.num_allowed_now} submissions remaining today.'; returns submit_result.message); kaggle/cli.py main (print(out, end=''); except HTTPError: print(e, file=sys.stderr); exit(1)); kagglesdk/kaggle_http_client.py _prepare_response (raise HTTPError(resp['message'])). Transcript outputs, e.g. 2026-09-26T21:15Z 'tail -2' shows only '2 submissions remaining today.'; 2026-09-28T12:15Z '0 submissions remaining today.'. Classifier test on 10 mock outputs: SUCCESS x2, NETWORK x3 (DNS 'Max retries exceeded', 429, rc 124), DAILY x1, HARD x2, UNKNOWN x2 (rc 0 with no line; odd text).
findings.action: Use nb_try v3 from night_checklist.md section P for every night submit. Delete R27N-3's 'Expect Successfully submitted' sentence from any prompt. Residual risk: if Kaggle returns the daily limit as HTTP 429, v3 retries it as network for 20 min, then pushes the user. That is harmless, because the list-first check makes it duplicate-safe.

findings.what: R28-A4 (iv) DAILY-LIMIT REGEX IS TOO WIDE AND IN THE WRONG ORDER. 'daily|allowance|submission limit|limit' contains a bare 'limit', so a transient 429 / 'rate limit' answer would exit 3 = STOP the whole batch with the user asleep. The same regex also sits after the success test, which never fires (R29F-2). Fix, in nb_try v3: test network first (incl. 'rate.?limit', 429, 'Max retries'), then daily without the bare 'limit', then hard fail. 'exceeded' is safe only because the network test ('Max retries exceeded') runs before it.

findings.action: Use v3's order as written. Do not re-add a bare 'limit'.

findings.what: ADMIT-EDGE SLACK SIGN IS INVERTED in two stored texts. R28-A4 (i) says 'first COMPLETE header <= 22:59:57Z + 210 s per failed attempt'. The logged CONTEXT 20:18Z (c) says 'a first COMPLETE header later than 22:59:57Z + 210 s per failed attempt = ?'. The ledger computes L_hi = header time + 210 s x failed attempts - submit (runtime_ledger.py l.210: first_result_upper = p.ts + RETRY_SLACK_S * failed_attempts). So the correct test is header + 210 s x f <= 22:59:57Z. The stored wording would admit a header up to 22:59:57Z + 210 f, i.e. L_hi up to 10.75 h + 0.058 f h. R27N-2 had the sign right for the 10.2 h mark. The texts differ only when the COMPLETE header carries >= 1 failed attempt AND lands within 210 f s of the edge (P << 1%), but the freeze is meant to be mechanical.
